title: The palace in your head
text: The technique {{1}} said to date back to a Greek poet, Simonides of Ceos, {{2}} stepped out of a banquet hall moments before the roof came down. {{3}} he noticed was that the victims could be identified by {{4}} each guest had been sitting, and the insight became an art: to remember a speech, you furnish an imagined palace and leave each point in a different room. To recall it, you simply walk {{5}} again. {{6}} is the power of place {{7}} every world memory champion still uses some version of the palace to memorise a shuffled deck of cards. The method works because the brain, {{8}} it never evolved a filing cabinet, did evolve superb spatial memory.

gaps.explanation: Fronted inversion: 'Such is the power that…'.

gaps.explanation: The result clause of 'Such is the power that'.

gaps.explanation: Concession inside the appositive clause: although.
